# WP3/WP4 shared isochrone grids — README

**Artifacts:** `data/processed/wp3_isochrones_parsec.parquet`,
`data/processed/wp3_isochrones_mist.parquet`
**Generated by:** `scripts/wp3_fetch_parsec.py`, `scripts/wp3_fetch_mist.py`
**Execution logs:** `provenance/wp3_parsec_fetch_execution.json`,
`provenance/wp3_mist_fetch_execution.json`

## Why this lives in WP3 but is shared with WP4

The execution plan couples WP3 and WP4 because both need the *same* isochrone
families with synthetic photometry in the *same* bands (Gaia G/BP/RP + 2MASS
JHK). WP3 reddens them to fit per-star extinction; WP4 fits ages/masses on the
de-reddened CMD. Generating them once here prevents a WP3/WP4 inconsistency
(e.g. different Gaia passband versions or metallicities producing incompatible
colours). **WP4 must consume these files, not regenerate its own.**

## Content

Both grids: solar metallicity, ages 1–10 Myr on a log grid (Δlog age = 0.05,
21 ages), **intrinsic (Av=0) absolute magnitudes**. Reddening is applied in-code
per R_V branch (`scripts/wp3_extinction_law.py`), so these files are the unreddened
templates.

Columns (standardised): `logAge, Mini, Mass, [logTe, logg, logL, label/phase],
G0, BP0, RP0, J0, H0, Ks0, age_Myr, family, track`. The `*0` magnitudes are
absolute Vega magnitudes.

| Family | Source | Version | Passbands | Rows | Masses |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PARSEC | CMD 3.9 (stev.oapd.inaf.it) | PARSEC v1.2S, Z=0.0152, YBCnewVega | Gaia EDR3 + 2MASS (queried separately, merged on logAge×Mini) | 6020 | 0.09–345 M☉ |
| MIST | mist.science interpolator | MIST v1.2, [Fe/H]=0, vvcrit=0.4, UBVRIplus bundle | Gaia EDR3 + 2MASS (single bundle) | 11213 | 0.10–295 M☉ |

Gaia EDR3 passbands are identical to DR3. The intrinsic colours of hot stars
agree between the two families to ≲0.05 mag (verified), consistent with the
expected family-insensitivity in the Rayleigh–Jeans tail.

## Reproduce

```
python3 scripts/wp3_fetch_parsec.py   # ~30 s, two CMD 3.9 POSTs
python3 scripts/wp3_fetch_mist.py     # ~1–2 min, one mist.science POST
```

Both fetchers POST directly over HTTPS (the CMD service silently drops POST
bodies on the http→https redirect) and require the full form field set incl.
`imf_file` (PARSEC returns an empty table otherwise).

## Model-branch note (binding downstream)

PARSEC and MIST disagree at the ~20–30% level for very young ages; per the global
conventions they are a **Class-E branch** and must be carried in parallel, never
averaged. WP3 extinction is reported using both families' template libraries
jointly in the broadband fit; the anchor intrinsic colours use the family
average (with the family spread recorded per star).
